title: Largest Element in an Array
problem: Given an array, find the largest element present in it.
idea: Scan the array once and keep updating the maximum value seen so far.
approach:
1. Assume the first element is the largest
2. Traverse the array from left to right
3. If the current element is greater than the stored maximum, update it
4. Return the maximum
dryRun:
`arr = [3,2,1,5,4]`

| i | x | max | action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 3 | 3 | initialize |
| 1 | 2 | 3 | no change |
| 2 | 1 | 3 | no change |
| 3 | 5 | 5 | update max |
| 4 | 4 | 5 | no change |

title: Second Largest Element in an Array without sorting
problem: Given an array, find the second largest distinct element without sorting the array.
idea: Keep track of the largest and second largest values while scanning the array once.
approach:
1. Initialize `largest` and `secondLargest`
2. If the current value is greater than `largest`, shift `largest` into `secondLargest`
3. Otherwise, if it is smaller than `largest` but greater than `secondLargest`, update `secondLargest`
4. Return `secondLargest`
dryRun:
`arr = [1,2,4,7,7,5]`

| x | largest | secondLargest | action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | -∞ | update largest |
| 2 | 2 | 1 | shift largest |
| 4 | 4 | 2 | shift largest |
| 7 | 7 | 4 | shift largest |
| 7 | 7 | 4 | duplicate largest |
| 5 | 7 | 5 | update second |

title: Check if the array is sorted
problem: Check whether an array is sorted in non-decreasing order.
idea: Compare every element with the previous element. If any current element is smaller, the array is not sorted.
approach:
1. Start from index 1
2. Compare `arr[i]` with `arr[i-1]`
3. If `arr[i] < arr[i-1]`, return false
4. If no violation is found, return true

title: Remove duplicates from Sorted array
problem: Given a sorted array, remove duplicates in-place and return the number of unique elements.
idea: Keep one pointer at the last unique element and another pointer scanning forward for new values.
approach:
1. Set `i = 0`
2. Traverse with `j` from index 1
3. If `arr[j] != arr[i]`, increment `i`
4. Copy `arr[j]` to `arr[i]`
5. Return `i + 1`

title: Left Rotate an array by one place
problem: Rotate an array to the left by one position.
idea: Store the first element, shift every other element one position left, then place the stored element at the end.
approach:
1. Store `arr[0]`
2. Shift elements from index 1 to the left
3. Place the stored first element at the last index
4. The array is now rotated by one position

title: Left rotate an array by D places
problem: Rotate an array to the left by `d` positions.
idea: Use the reversal technique: reverse the first `d` elements, reverse the remaining elements, then reverse the entire array.
approach:
1. Compute `d = d % n`
2. Reverse indices `0` to `d-1`
3. Reverse indices `d` to `n-1`
4. Reverse the complete array
5. The array is left rotated by `d`
dryRun:
`arr = [1,2,3,4,5], d = 2`

| step | array |
|---|---|
| reverse first 2 | [2,1,3,4,5] |
| reverse remaining | [2,1,5,4,3] |
| reverse all | [3,4,5,1,2] |

title: Move Zeros to end
problem: Move all zeroes to the end of the array while keeping the order of non-zero elements unchanged.
idea: Use one pointer to mark the position where the next non-zero element should be placed.
approach:
1. Set pointer `j = 0`
2. Traverse the array
3. Whenever a non-zero element is found, swap it with `arr[j]`
4. Increment `j`
5. All zeroes automatically move to the end

title: Linear Search
problem: Find the index of a target element in an array using linear search.
idea: Check every element from left to right until the target is found.
approach:
1. Start from index 0
2. Compare each element with the target
3. If equal, return its index
4. If the target is never found, return -1
dryRun:
`arr = [5,3,7,1], target = 7`

| i | x | action |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 5 | not target |
| 1 | 3 | not target |
| 2 | 7 | found → return 2 |

title: Find the Union
problem: Find the union of two sorted arrays without including duplicate elements.
idea: Use two pointers to compare both sorted arrays and add only the smaller unique element each time.
approach:
1. Set `i = 0` and `j = 0`
2. Compare elements from both arrays
3. Add the smaller element if it is not already added
4. If both are equal, add it once and move both pointers
5. Add any remaining unique elements

title: Find missing number in an array
problem: Given an array containing distinct numbers from `0` to `n` with one number missing, find the missing number.
idea: XOR all indices and all array elements. Equal values cancel out, leaving only the missing number.
approach:
1. Start with `xor = n`
2. For every index `i`
3. XOR `xor` with `i`
4. XOR `xor` with `arr[i]`
5. Return the final XOR value

title: Maximum Consecutive Ones
problem: Given a binary array, find the maximum number of consecutive `1`s.
idea: Keep a current count of consecutive ones and reset it whenever a zero appears.
approach:
1. Set `count = 0` and `max = 0`
2. Traverse the array
3. If the element is 1, increment `count`
4. Otherwise reset `count = 0`
5. Update `max` after each step

title: Find the number that appears once, and other numbers twice
problem: Every element appears twice except one element. Find the element that appears only once.
idea: XOR of two equal numbers is zero, and XOR with zero gives the original number. So all pairs cancel out.
approach:
1. Initialize `xor = 0`
2. Traverse all elements
3. XOR every element with `xor`
4. Duplicate values cancel each other
5. Return the remaining value

title: Longest subarray with given sum K (positives)
problem: Given an array of positive integers and a value `k`, find the length of the longest subarray whose sum equals `k`.
idea: Because all values are positive, expand the right pointer to increase the sum and move the left pointer when the sum becomes too large.
approach:
1. Set `left = 0` and `sum = 0`
2. Expand the right pointer and add elements
3. While `sum > k`, remove elements from the left
4. If `sum == k`, update the maximum length
5. Continue until the end of the array

title: Longest subarray with sum K (Positives + Negatives)
problem: Given an array containing positive and negative numbers, find the length of the longest subarray whose sum equals `k`.
idea: If the current prefix sum is `sum`, then a previous prefix sum of `sum - k` means the subarray between them has sum `k`.
approach:
1. Maintain a running prefix sum
2. If the prefix sum equals `k`, update the answer
3. Check whether `sum - k` exists in the map
4. Use its earliest index to calculate the longest length
5. Store each prefix sum only the first time it appears
dryRun:
`arr = [1,-1,5,-2,3], k = 3`

| i | x | prefix sum | action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | 1 | store 1→0 |
| 1 | -1 | 0 | store 0→1 |
| 2 | 5 | 5 | need 2 not found |
| 3 | -2 | 3 | prefix itself = 3 → length 4 |
| 4 | 3 | 6 | need 3 found |

title: 2Sum Problem
problem: Given an array and a target, return the indices of two numbers whose sum equals the target.
idea: Store `value → index` while scanning. For each value `x`, check whether `target - x` already exists.
approach:
1. Create an empty HashMap
2. For each element, calculate `need = target - nums[i]`
3. If `need` exists in the map, return both indices
4. Otherwise store the current value and index

title: Sort an array of 0's 1's and 2's
problem: Sort an array containing only `0`, `1`, and `2` without using a sorting algorithm.
idea: Use three pointers: `low` for 0s, `mid` for scanning, and `high` for 2s.
approach:
1. Set `low = 0`, `mid = 0`, `high = n - 1`
2. If `arr[mid] == 0`, swap with `low`
3. If `arr[mid] == 1`, move `mid`
4. If `arr[mid] == 2`, swap with `high`
5. Continue while `mid <= high`

title: Majority Element (>n/2 times)
problem: Find the element that appears more than `n/2` times in the array.
idea: Keep a candidate and a count. Equal elements increase the count and different elements decrease it.
approach:
1. Set `count = 0`
2. If count becomes 0, choose the current element as candidate
3. If current element equals candidate, increment count
4. Otherwise decrement count
5. Return the candidate

title: Kadane's Algorithm, maximum subarray sum
problem: Find the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray.
idea: Keep a running sum. If the running sum becomes worse than starting fresh from the current element, restart it.
approach:
1. Set `sum = 0`
2. Add each element to the running sum
3. Update the maximum sum
4. If `sum < 0`, reset it to 0
5. Continue until the end

title: Print subarray with maximum subarray sum
problem: Find the contiguous subarray having the maximum sum and return that subarray.
idea: Use Kadane's Algorithm while also storing the start and end indices of the best subarray.
approach:
1. Keep a running sum
2. When starting a new sum, remember its starting index
3. If the current sum becomes the maximum, save start and end
4. If the sum becomes negative, reset it
5. Return the subarray between saved indices

title: Stock Buy and Sell
problem: Given stock prices for each day, find the maximum profit from one buy and one sell.
idea: Track the lowest price seen so far and calculate the profit if selling on the current day.
approach:
1. Set the minimum price to the first price
2. Traverse from the second day
3. Calculate `profit = price - minPrice`
4. Update the maximum profit
5. Update the minimum price

title: Rearrange the array in alternating positive and negative items
problem: Rearrange the array so positive and negative numbers appear alternately, starting with a positive number.
idea: Place positive numbers at even indices and negative numbers at odd indices.
approach:
1. Create an answer array
2. Set positive index to 0
3. Set negative index to 1
4. Put positives at even indices
5. Put negatives at odd indices

title: Next Permutation
problem: Transform the array into the next lexicographically greater permutation.
idea: Find the first decreasing point from the right, swap it with the next greater element, then reverse the suffix.
approach:
1. Find the first index `i` from the right where `nums[i] < nums[i+1]`
2. If found, find the smallest greater element from the right
3. Swap them
4. Reverse the suffix after `i`
5. If no such index exists, reverse the whole array
dryRun:
`arr = [1,2,3]`

| step | array | action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [1,2,3] | break point = index 1 |
| 2 | [1,3,2] | swap 2 and 3 |
| 3 | [1,3,2] | suffix already smallest |

title: Leaders in an Array problem
problem: Find all elements that are greater than or equal to every element on their right.
idea: Traverse from right to left while keeping track of the maximum element seen so far.
approach:
1. Start from the last element
2. Keep `maxRight`
3. If the current element is at least `maxRight`, it is a leader
4. Update `maxRight`
5. Reverse the result at the end

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence in an Array
problem: Find the length of the longest sequence of consecutive integers in an unsorted array.
idea: Use a HashSet and only start counting when the previous number does not exist.
approach:
1. Insert all elements into a HashSet
2. For each number, check if `x - 1` exists
3. If not, `x` is the start of a sequence
4. Keep checking `x + 1`, `x + 2`, and so on
5. Track the maximum sequence length

title: Set Matrix Zeros
problem: If any cell in a matrix is zero, set its entire row and column to zero.
idea: Use the first row and first column as markers so no extra matrix is required.
approach:
1. Check whether the first row contains zero
2. Check whether the first column contains zero
3. Use first row and first column to mark zero rows and columns
4. Set marked cells to zero
5. Finally update the first row and first column

title: Rotate Matrix by 90 degrees
problem: Rotate an `n × n` matrix by 90 degrees clockwise in-place.
idea: Transpose the matrix and then reverse every row.
approach:
1. Transpose the matrix across the main diagonal
2. Reverse every row
3. The matrix becomes rotated 90 degrees clockwise

title: Print the matrix in spiral manner
problem: Return all matrix elements in spiral order.
idea: Maintain four boundaries: top, bottom, left, and right, and shrink them after each traversal.
approach:
1. Traverse the top row from left to right
2. Traverse the right column from top to bottom
3. Traverse the bottom row from right to left
4. Traverse the left column from bottom to top
5. Move the boundaries inward

title: Count subarrays with given sum
problem: Count the number of contiguous subarrays whose sum equals `k`.
idea: If the current prefix sum is `sum`, every earlier prefix sum equal to `sum - k` creates a valid subarray.
approach:
1. Store prefix-sum frequencies in a HashMap
2. Start with `0 → 1`
3. Add each element to the running sum
4. Add the frequency of `sum - k` to the answer
5. Increase the frequency of the current sum

title: Pascal's Triangle
problem: Generate the first `numRows` rows of Pascal's Triangle.
idea: Every element is the sum of the two elements directly above it. The first and last element of every row are always `1`.
approach:
1. Create an empty result list
2. For each row, start with `1`
3. Generate the next value using the previous value
4. Add the completed row to the result
5. Repeat until all rows are generated

title: Majority Element (n/3 times)
problem: Find all elements that appear more than `n/3` times in the array.
idea: At most two elements can appear more than `n/3` times, so maintain two candidates and two counters.
approach:
1. Maintain two candidates and their counts
2. If the current number matches a candidate, increase its count
3. If a count is zero, replace that candidate
4. Otherwise decrease both counts
5. Verify both candidates in a second pass

title: 3-Sum Problem
problem: Find all unique triplets in the array whose sum is `0`.
idea: Sort the array, fix one element, then use two pointers to find the remaining two elements.
approach:
1. Sort the array
2. Fix one element at index `i`
3. Use `left = i + 1` and `right = n - 1`
4. If the sum is too small, move left
5. If the sum is too large, move right
6. If the sum is zero, store the triplet and skip duplicates

title: 4-Sum Problem
problem: Find all unique quadruplets whose sum equals the target.
idea: Sort the array, fix two elements, then use two pointers to find the remaining pair.
approach:
1. Sort the array
2. Fix the first element using `i`
3. Fix the second element using `j`
4. Use two pointers for the remaining part
5. Compare the total sum with target
6. Store valid quadruplets and skip duplicates

title: Largest Subarray with 0 Sum
problem: Find the length of the longest subarray whose sum is `0`.
idea: If the same prefix sum appears twice, the elements between those two positions have sum `0`.
approach:
1. Maintain a running prefix sum
2. If the prefix sum becomes `0`, update answer with `i + 1`
3. If the prefix sum was seen before, calculate the distance
4. Otherwise store its first index
5. Track the maximum length
dryRun:
`arr = [9,-3,3,-1,6,-5]`

| i | prefix sum | action |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 9 | store 9→0 |
| 1 | 6 | store 6→1 |
| 2 | 9 | seen at 0 → length 2 |
| 3 | 8 | store 8→3 |
| 4 | 14 | store 14→4 |
| 5 | 9 | seen at 0 → length 5 |

title: Count number of subarrays with given xor K
problem: Count the number of subarrays whose XOR equals `k`.
idea: If the current prefix XOR is `xor`, then a previous prefix XOR of `xor ^ k` forms a subarray with XOR `k`.
approach:
1. Store prefix XOR frequencies in a HashMap
2. Start with `0 → 1`
3. Update the running XOR
4. Compute `need = xor ^ k`
5. Add the frequency of `need`
6. Store the current XOR

title: Merge Overlapping Subintervals
problem: Merge all overlapping intervals and return the non-overlapping result.
idea: Sort intervals by starting point. If the next interval starts before the current interval ends, merge them.
approach:
1. Sort intervals by starting value
2. Start with the first interval
3. Compare the next interval with the current merged interval
4. If they overlap, extend the end
5. Otherwise store the current interval and start a new one

title: Merge two sorted arrays without extra space
problem: Merge two sorted arrays without using an extra array.
idea: Treat both arrays as one virtual array and compare elements at a decreasing gap, similar to Shell Sort.
approach:
1. Set gap to the ceiling of half the combined length
2. Compare elements `gap` positions apart
3. Swap if they are in the wrong order
4. Reduce the gap
5. Stop when gap becomes zero

title: Find the repeating and missing number
problem: An array contains numbers from `1` to `n`. One number is missing and one number appears twice. Find both.
idea: Compare the actual sum and square sum with the expected values to form two equations.
approach:
1. Calculate expected sum `1 + 2 + ... + n`
2. Calculate expected square sum
3. Calculate actual sum and actual square sum
4. Let `x` be repeating and `y` be missing
5. Solve the two equations to get `x` and `y`
dryRun:
`arr = [3,1,2,5,3]`

Expected numbers: `[1,2,3,4,5]`

| value | result |
|---|---|
| repeating | 3 |
| missing | 4 |

title: Count Inversions
problem: Count pairs `(i, j)` such that `i < j` and `arr[i] > arr[j]`.
idea: Use Merge Sort. During merging, if a left element is greater than a right element, all remaining left elements form inversions.
approach:
1. Divide the array using Merge Sort
2. Count inversions in the left half
3. Count inversions in the right half
4. Count cross inversions while merging
5. Add all counts together

title: Reverse Pairs
problem: Count pairs `(i, j)` such that `i < j` and `nums[i] > 2 * nums[j]`.
idea: Use Merge Sort. Before merging two sorted halves, count how many right-side values satisfy the reverse-pair condition for each left-side value.
approach:
1. Divide the array using Merge Sort
2. Recursively count reverse pairs in both halves
3. Before merging, use a pointer in the right half
4. For every left element, count all right elements satisfying `nums[i] > 2 * nums[j]`
5. Merge the two sorted halves

title: Maximum Product Subarray
problem: Find the contiguous subarray with the largest product.
idea: Negative numbers can turn a small negative product into a large positive product. Scan from both left and right to handle this.
approach:
1. Maintain a prefix product
2. Maintain a suffix product
3. Reset either product to 1 if it becomes 0
4. Multiply from both ends
5. Keep track of the maximum product seen

title: Selection Sort
problem: Sort an array in ascending order using Selection Sort.
idea: For each position, find the smallest element from the unsorted part and place it at the current position.
approach:
1. Start from the first index
2. Find the minimum element in the remaining unsorted array
3. Swap it with the current element
4. Repeat until the array is sorted
dryRun:
`arr = [4,2,1,3]`

| pass | array | action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [1,2,4,3] | place 1 at index 0 |
| 2 | [1,2,4,3] | 2 already correct |
| 3 | [1,2,3,4] | place 3 at index 2 |

title: Bubble Sort
problem: Sort an array in ascending order using Bubble Sort.
idea: Compare adjacent elements and swap them when they are in the wrong order. After each pass, the largest remaining element moves to the end.
approach:
1. Start from the beginning of the array
2. Compare adjacent elements
3. Swap if the left element is greater
4. Repeat for every pass
5. Stop early if no swaps happen
dryRun:
`arr = [4,2,1,3]`

| pass | array | action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [2,1,3,4] | 4 moves to the end |
| 2 | [1,2,3,4] | remaining elements sorted |
| 3 | [1,2,3,4] | no swap → stop |

title: Insertion Sort
problem: Sort an array in ascending order using Insertion Sort.
idea: Keep the left part sorted and insert each new element into its correct position.
approach:
1. Treat the first element as sorted
2. Pick the next element
3. Shift all larger elements one position to the right
4. Insert the picked element in its correct position
5. Repeat for the whole array

title: Merge Sort
problem: Sort an array in ascending order using Merge Sort.
idea: Divide the array into halves until single elements remain, then merge the halves back in sorted order.
approach:
1. Find the middle index
2. Recursively sort the left half
3. Recursively sort the right half
4. Merge both sorted halves
5. Continue until the complete array is sorted
dryRun:
`arr = [4,2,1,3]`

| step | parts | action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [4,2] [1,3] | divide |
| 2 | [4] [2] [1] [3] | divide again |
| 3 | [2,4] [1,3] | merge small parts |
| 4 | [1,2,3,4] | final merge |

title: Recursive Bubble Sort
problem: Sort an array using Bubble Sort implemented with recursion.
idea: Perform one Bubble Sort pass to move the largest element to the end, then recursively sort the remaining first `n-1` elements.
approach:
1. If only one element remains, stop
2. Perform one bubble pass
3. Move the largest element to the end
4. Recursively sort the first `n-1` elements
5. Continue until the whole array is sorted
dryRun:
`arr = [4,2,1,3]`

| call | array | action |
|---|---|---|
| n=4 | [2,1,3,4] | 4 moves to end |
| n=3 | [1,2,3,4] | 3 reaches correct place |
| n=2 | [1,2,3,4] | first two sorted |

title: Recursive Insertion Sort
problem: Sort an array using Insertion Sort implemented with recursion.
idea: Recursively sort the first `n-1` elements, then insert the last element into its correct position.
approach:
1. If one element remains, stop
2. Recursively sort the first `n-1` elements
3. Store the last element
4. Shift larger sorted elements to the right
5. Insert the stored element at its correct position

title: Quick Sort
problem: Sort an array in ascending order using Quick Sort.
idea: Choose a pivot, place smaller elements on its left and larger elements on its right, then recursively sort both parts.
approach:
1. Choose a pivot
2. Partition the array around the pivot
3. Put the pivot in its correct sorted position
4. Recursively sort the left part
5. Recursively sort the right part
dryRun:
`arr = [4,2,1,3]`

| step | array | action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [2,1,3,4] | pivot 3 placed correctly |
| 2 | [1,2,3,4] | sort left part |
| 3 | [1,2,3,4] | right part already sorted |
time: Average O(n log n), Worst O(n²)
